interpretation: The passages discuss the same adanta kathadi/Curadi lexical series and expressly exemplify the two finite forms. They do not introduce a distinct lexical entry, meaning, prefix, or a second sanadi operation for these examples.

The neighboring Vanta/Lanja paragraph explains a-deletion displacement, strengthening, and puK for those entries. I do not treat that neighboring derivational explanation as an independent proof of every kathadi derivation; the exact kath/gan forms are instead directly printed in the separate Sakatayana sentence.

Curadi class-intrinsic nic is already part of ordinary conjugation (and present in both saved tasks at rule 3.1.25); it is not an extra user-selected causative coordinate. The source presents puK as an attributed alternative within this discussion.

The public prompts ask for one valid form and supply no grammatical-school restriction. On this evidence, rejecting these two exact printed alternatives solely by imposing an unstated school is unsupported.
The commentary identifies Sakatayana as a rsi. The finding does not require equating this attribution with a wholly different grammatical system or proving common attestation in literary usage.
